summary: When the hero rejects naming the chaotic artifact Stormbringer, C chooses how many letters to scuff with the display RNG, then wipeout_text uses the core game RNG for character positions and replacement choices. JS injects the display RNG into wipeout_text, so it omits those core calls and produces a different scuffed name.

source.branch: If artifact_name recognizes a canonical artifact name and restrict_name or exist_artifact rejects this object/name pairing, C copies the canonical name, calls rnd_on_display_rng(2) only for the count, then calls wipeout_text(bufp, count, 0). Since seed is zero, engrave.c:wipeout_text uses process rn2 for character positions, rubout selection and replacement choice. The selected chaotic Rogue rejects Stormbringer for a runed broadsword; the saved trace first loses those core draws at step 117.
callers: do_name.c:docallcmd case 'i' selects an object and calls do_oname; js/do_name.js:docallcmd dispatches the same naming menu.
dependencies: engrave.c:wipeout_text is the existing void degradation helper; C discards its return (there is none). js/engrave.js already defaults its random provider to the process rn2/rnd stream. The caller must not override it with rn2_on_display_rng.

evidence: The saved accepted v55 evaluation has 157/159 screens, 2305/2311 RNG values, and 159/159 cursors matching, with error null.

Fresh replay at b3a095e1bf941171ac53635f2c7697a4b47daef2 first differs at zero-based step 117 in the RNG stream: C calls rn2(12)=9 from wipeout_text(engrave.c:134), while JS does not call the core RNG. The next screen differs at step 118, row 0 column 16. Receipt: /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-0RRVVq/receipt.json.

upstream/src/do_name.c:349 calls wipeout_text(bufp, rnd_on_display_rng(2), 0): the count uses the display stream, but the zero seed delegates per-character draws to engrave.c:wipeout_text. upstream/src/engrave.c:120-190 uses rn2 for character position, rubout choice, and replacement selection when seed is zero.

js/do_name.js:857-859 currently passes rnd_on_display_rng(2) for the count and also injects rn2_on_display_rng as wipeout_text's random.rn2. js/engrave.js:1314+ correctly uses its default process rn2 provider when no random override is supplied. Prior do_oname completion evidence at GOALS.json's do_name.c port records full function review; this task repairs only that caller RNG binding.
